notes: iris-3b Turbo (speridlabs/iris-3b rev adc05b9, Apache-2.0; text encoder Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct rev ebb281e): text to a 768x768 image, exported with litert-torch 0.9.4 and stored with ai-edge-quantizer 0.9.0's full_fp16_recipe (the form H), published as litert-community/iris-3b-Turbo-LiteRT main 743fd20a (last modified 2026-10-21T19:14:17.000Z; anonymous Hub API read 2026-10-22 JST: the 22 LFS files under model/ carry the sha256 of model/SHA256SUMS, and the git blob ids of iris3b_config.json, iris_tokenizer.json and SHA256SUMS equal the staged files). A pipeline record: `artifact` is the pipeline config the engine opens; it names the 20 graphs in order and sets GPU, FP32, P1 and no program cache for each. The files of one image are the bytes of model/SHA256SUMS: the text-encoder graphs iris_te_c00..c11_f16w (one per hidden-state tap of Qwen3-VL-4B's decoder), the DiT graphs iris_dit_{adapter,dual0,dual1,dual2,single0,single1,single2,pixel}_f16w_dit, the bf16 embedding table, the host tensor pack and the tokenizer. P1 = each graph is loaded, run and closed in turn: 41 compiles per image (12 + 1 + 4 steps x 7). Each image is scored against the all-fp32 upstream PyTorch image of the same noise (score_image.py: PSNR and SSIM on (x+1)/2); the pre-registered bar is PSNR >= 35 dB and SSIM >= 0.98 on all three prompts (apple, punct_num, japanese). A pipeline check, so output_match stays null and the scores are metrics; latency_p50_ms stays null and the image walls are metrics (first_image_wall_ms is the published speed figure for this phone). Harness: the engine app r4 (build 3; the zoo sample is build 4 of the same engine) in its BenchActivity through a benchmark script in generic mode: the three prompts back to back in one process, starting warm (thermal status 1, no caps); the chain pushed the files and read their sha256 back. Not rows here: the zoo sample's run of the same form on this phone the same day (212.6 s for its first image after the install, from thermal status 0; its three images equal these byte for byte), the TE-on-CPU form and the P4 prefetch form (the speed comparison).
quantization: fp16 weights: the fully-connected weights are stored as fp16 with a DEQUANTIZE in front of each; activations are fp32 (the Hub card, 'How it runs'); the token-embedding table is bf16 on the host
